about: The solubility of carbon dioxide in water at a total pressure of 101.325 kPa and of 500 kPa, 10 to 80 degC: Table 3 of Carroll, Slupsky and Mather (1991), as printed (mole fraction x 1000). The authors calculated these values from their Henry's-law correlation of the low-pressure data of about 100 experimental investigations, graded against each other (Figures 2 to 5 compare it with the measurements); they write that the tables 'should not be considered as a substitute for experimental data'. So this is an evaluated correlation of measured data, independent of IAPWS G7-04, not a measurement. The 0 degC row is left out: CHEPTA's Henry's law constant of CO2 (IAPWS G7-04) starts at 274.19 K. Used by test/henry-components.test.js (proposal 0017).

reference.citation: J. J. Carroll, J. D. Slupsky, A. E. Mather, The Solubility of Carbon Dioxide in Water at Low Pressure, J. Phys. Chem. Ref. Data 20 (1991) 1201-1209
reference.access: Free to read: reprint hosted by NIST (Standard Reference Data); read 2026-11-04
reference.tables: Table 3, p. 1208, columns 101.325 and 500 kPa, rows 10 to 80 degC (the table's header says 'CO' for carbon dioxide, a misprint: the article is about CO2)

units.x: mole fraction of CO2 in the liquid x 1000
